semi-retractivity. Clarification: This stress is called “semi-retractivity” because it was assumed the leftward shift of the stress in the prefixed forms of the l-participle and aorist from the verbs of the Proto-Slavic accent paradigm b. In fact, the Proto-Slavic semi-retractivity is a consequence of the phonological prohibition on the rightward shift of stress from dominant roots to recessive suffixes in wordforms in which the stressed syllable was not the initial one.
